previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, chronic systolic heart failure, and gastroparesis was admitted due to hypertensive urgency and altered mental status. He presented with nausea, vomiting, and confusion, with an initial blood pressure of 235/107 mmHg. The elevated blood pressure and volume overload were managed with intravenous nitroglycerin and emergent hemodialysis, which improved his mental status and stabilized his condition. Imaging studies, including head CT and MRI, showed no acute intracranial abnormalities, with findings consistent with chronic changes. His confusion was attributed to metabolic encephalopathy likely exacerbated by hypertension and polypharmacy. Medications were adjusted, including restarting hydralazine, modifying insulin dosing, and changing hiccup management by stopping chlorpromazine and reducing baclofen dose. The patient improved clinically, returned to his baseline mental status, and was discharged home in stable condition with updated medication instructions and follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
# AMS in setting of h/o anoxic encephalopathy / Seizures: When 
patient was admitted patient had an extensive work up for change 
in mental status including CT ___ and MR ___ which were both 
negative for acute processes. No LP was performed because pt did 
not have meningeal signs. As patient was complaining of Chest 
pain and had troponin elevation over his baseline troponin of 
about 0.2 given his CKD, it was assumed that an NSTEMI was 
likely responsible for this change in mental status (see below). 
Patient's mental status improved until ___ when patient became 
minimally responsive and was noted to have a flat expression and 
bilateral contrcations in the upper and lower extremities. 
Patient was started on Ativan and then dilantin and improved 
remarkably. Neurology was consulted, and although EEG was not 
consistent with seizures, the Neuro team felt that the patient 
was indeed having seizures because encephalopathy can decrease 
the sensitivity of EEGs and he responded so well to 
anti-epileptics. Repeat MRI demonstrated no new changes. A 
gadolinium study was not pursued because it was thought that the 
risks outweighed the benefits of the renal-toxicity. The seizure 
etiology likely had to do with the patient's underlying brain 
injury from his PEA arrest and known frontal lobe lesion in the 
setting of stopping Carbamazepine for hiccups (which was not 
working for that indication, and was never at a therapeutic 
level) and adding several other medications in a short time 
period that can lower seizure threshold (including Zofran, 
baclofen and haldol). In retrospect, it is possible that his 
hiccups could potentially have been related to diaphragmatic 
seizures in addition to gastritis (see below). Patient did very 
well on Dilantin, even though his serum levels were 
subtherapetuic and this medication was continued at discharge 
with Neurology follow up. 
.
# NSTEMI/CP: Patient was noted to have CP on admission and a 
slight troponin elevation over his baseline, but no ECG changes. 
Patient was maximally medically managed for coronary disease 
(beta blocker, aspirin, statin) with tight glucose control.
.
# Gastrparesis:  EGD on this admission showed significant 
residual stomach contents. Patient had a period of 4 days during 
the admission where he did not have a bm. KUB ___ showed 
copious stool, but no obstruction. His diet was withheld and 
patient stooled when lactulose was added to his bowel regimen 
and had at least QOD bms after that. Mr. ___ was continued on 
a diabetic Diet regular (diabtetic), as well as reglan 5mg QID, 
and senna, colace, ducolax, and lactulose for bowel regimen. 
.
# DM I: Controlling Mr. ___ sugars at home has been a 
problem for some time because he has had limited services. To 
this end, the medical team in conjunction with with ___ 
consult found a regimen that was simple but continued to control 
Mr. ___ blood sugars even 2 hours after meals. Hg A1c was 
less than 7 during the hospital admission, and blood sugar was 
generally less than 140 but greater than 60. Patient was 
discharged on Lantus 8 qam and encouraged to take regular po 
intake, without much change in his overall diet. 
.
# HTN: BP acutely worsened when patient was unable to take po 
medications during his seizure. He has minimial vascular accsss, 
so no IV medications were given for hypertension. Although he 
occasionally became non-symptomatically hypotensive after 
dialysis, patient overall did well on Metoprolol and Loartan 
through the majority of his hospital stay. 
.
# h/o Hiccups: Unclear etiology, but likely ___ gastroperesis, 
and as such patient was placed on a twice daily PPI. Could also 
have been a manifestation of his seizures (see above). Baclofen, 
thorazine and tegretol were stopped given decreased seizure 
threshhold with these medications. Patient's hiccups disappeared 
once seizures were controlled with Dilantin. 
.
# Erosive gastritis: Patient's bx are negative for malignancy. 
He was continued on a  PPI BID.
.
# ESRD: Patient has history of CKD 5 on HD MWF in ___. 
Patient's ESRD is secondary to diabetic nephropathy. He received 
dialysis MWF during his hospital stay with Dr. ___ 
nephrology. 
.
# Depression: No active issues. Continued Amitriptyline.

Discharge Instructions:
You were hospitalized because you had some confusion.  After 
performing several tests, it appears that the source of your 
confusion was likely secondary to a seizure. For your seizure 
you have been started on DILANTIN. It is very important that you 
take your DILANTIN every day. Missing doses of DILANTIN can 
result in seizures, confusion and even death.

Additionally, you also had several tests performed that show 
that you did not have an infection in your blood. We think you 
may have had a mild heart attack and several changes were made 
to your medication regimen, as below.

To ensure acute and timely insulin administration you have been 
started on a once a day dose of LANTUS.

We examined a cause for your hiccups and discovered you have 
severe erosive esophagitis that is likely causing some of your 
chest discomfort. Your protonix was increased, as below, to help 
treat this. You were tried on Tegretol but this did not help 
your hiccups.

If you experience any fevers, chills, vomiting, chest pain, 
shortness of air, or any other concerning symptoms, please call 
your primary care provider or return to the emergency room.

your gastritis.

There is a focal isoechoic collection noticed adjacent to the brachial artery
without significant arterial compression with a small area of increased
echogenicity in its superior aspect.  This is consistent with an aging
hematoma and there were previously findings consistent with a pseudoaneurysm

ageing hematoma was measured as 1.35 AP x 2.38 TR cm in size.  The following

significant stenosis in this area.  This may result in pulsatility of the
graft, prolonged bleeding after dialysis or increased pressures as well as

evaluation by angiographic imaging may be helpful.

anastomosis which should be clinically correlated as described and maybe
further evaluated by angiographic imaging with intervention as indicated.
Correlation with parameters such as prolonged bleeding during dialysis, graft
pulsatility, diminished flow etc is recommended.
